message.content:
Here’s a concise overview of key Texas traffic laws and regulations that drivers should know: | Area | Key Points | Practical Tips | |------|------------|----------------| | **Speed Limits** | • Posted limits vary by road type (e.g., 55 mph on rural interstates, 45 mph on urban interstates).
• “No‑limit” highways (e.g., I‑10, I‑35) still have a 75 mph cap in most counties. | • Always obey posted signs; speed cameras and automated enforcement are common. | | **Seat‑belt & Child‑seat Requirements** | • All occupants must wear seat belts.
• Children under 8 must be in a child safety seat or booster. | • Check the seat‑belt reminder light; it turns on if a belt isn’t fastened. | | **Cell‑phone Use** | • Hand‑held texting or calling is illegal while driving.
• Hands‑free devices are allowed. | • Use voice‑activated features or pull over if you need to make a call. | | **Alcohol & Drug Limits** | • Blood Alcohol Concentration (BAC) limit is 0.08 % for all drivers.
• Zero‑tolerance for drivers under 21. | • If you’re unsure, stay off the road. | | **DUI Penalties** | • First offense: up to 90 days jail, $2,000 fine, 1‑year license suspension.
• Subsequent offenses carry harsher penalties. | • Consider a pre‑trial diversion program if you’re a first‑time offender. | | **Traffic Signal & Stop‑Sign Rules** | • Red lights mean stop; green means proceed only if the intersection is clear.
• Yellow lights require safe completion of the turn or stop. | • Use the “stop‑and‑look” rule at four‑way stops to avoid rear‑end collisions. | | **Right‑of‑Way** | • Pedestrians always have right‑of‑way at crosswalks.
• Emergency vehicles with flashing lights have priority. | • Yield to emergency vehicles even if you’re not in the lane they’re traveling. | | **Lane‑Changing & Passing** | • Use turn signals at least 100 ft before changing lanes.
• Do not pass on the right unless the vehicle ahead is turning left. | • Keep a safe following distance (at least 2 seconds). | | **School‑Zone Speed Limits** | • 25 mph during school hours; 15 mph when children are present. | • Pay attention to flashing signs and school buses stopping. | | **Parking Regulations** | • No parking within 20 ft of a stop sign or crosswalk.
• No parking on sidewalks or in front of driveways. | • Use designated parking lots whenever possible. | | **Vehicle Equipment** | • Headlights must be on from sunset to sunrise.
• Tires must have at least 2 / 32 in. tread depth. | • Perform a quick pre‑trip check before long drives. | | **Insurance Requirements** | • Minimum liability coverage: 30/60/25 (bodily injury per person, bodily injury per accident, property damage). | • Keep proof of insurance in the vehicle at all times. | ### Quick Reference Resources - **Texas Department of Transportation (TxDOT)** – Official traffic law updates and driver handbooks. - **Texas Motor Vehicle Commission (TxMVC)** – Licensing, registration, and insurance requirements. - **Texas Highway Patrol** – Enforcement guidelines and public safety advisories. Feel free to let me know if you’d like more detail on any specific area—such as toll roads, commercial driver regulations, or recent legislative changes!
